contradicting_evidence: ETH/BTC rose 0.43% during the latest completed hour while ETH declined less than BTC, indicating relative resilience.
Breadth improved by two percentage points since the prior packet, although only 30% of constituents advanced.
Large-alt proxies substantially outperformed BTC, and anchor funding was not uniformly positive; an uninterrupted downside move or crowded-long liquidation cannot be assumed.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Further downside probing or a weak rebound followed by renewed selling is favored over sustained recovery. ETH and selected large alts may remain relatively resilient without producing positive absolute returns or broad altcoin transmission. A reflex bounce remains plausible, so the forecast is not for a monotonic decline.
falsification_conditions: BTC and ETH sustain recovery of the latest hourly losses across subsequent completed candles, supported by stronger spot buying rather than price gains driven mainly by rising open interest.
Participation expands durably alongside positive large- and mid-alt median returns, replacing the current pattern of relative outperformance during absolute declines.
missing_evidence: Subsequent completed candles are needed to distinguish continuation from a one-hour downside excursion.
Current order-book conditions, liquidation flows and synchronized funding are unavailable.
supporting_evidence: The latest completed hour shows BTC down 0.87% and ETH down 0.43%; BTC taker-buy quote share was only 42.1%, consistent with sell-led pressure.
BTC and ETH both registered price down with open interest up, increasing positioning fragility without identifying whether new exposure is predominantly long or short.
Freshest Top-100 proxy breadth shows 30 advancers versus 69 decliners and a median 24h return of approximately -0.98%. These are one breadth-family observation, not independent votes.
Mid-alt and small-alt proxy medians were approximately -1.27% and -1.19%, respectively, limiting evidence that relative resilience is becoming broad recovery.
